name: claude-viewer
description: Inspect your agent's grounding files. View content, size, token estimates.

enumDescriptions: Characters divided by 4 — the published rule of thumb, and what this panel has always shown.
The same rule times 1.35, adjusted for Claude's current tokenizer, which runs denser than 4 characters per token.
claudeViewer.tokens.estimator.markdownDescription: Which approximation every **est. tokens** figure in the panel uses. Nothing here runs a real tokenizer — the point of an estimate is that it costs one division — so both options are claims, and `anthropic` is the one adjusted for how Claude actually reads text. Budgets are read in whichever units this produces.

enumDescriptions: The panel's own palette, in whichever polarity your editor is in — dark theme, dark panel.
The panel's dark palette, whatever the editor is set to.
The panel's light palette, whatever the editor is set to.
Every color read from the active VS Code theme, which is what the panel did before it had palettes of its own.
claudeViewer.theme.mode.markdownDescription: Which palette the panel draws in. `auto`, the default, draws the panel's own palette in whichever polarity your editor is in — dark theme, dark panel. `inherit` instead reads every color off the active VS Code theme, which is what the panel did before it had palettes of its own. `dark` and `light` pick one outright.

claudeViewer.budgets.skills.description.markdownDescription: Estimated tokens a skill's name and description should cost. This pair sits in the system prompt on **every request**, whether or not the skill ever runs. Set to `0` to turn the check off.

claudeViewer.budgets.skills.content.markdownDescription: Estimated tokens a skill's whole `SKILL.md` should cost. This is read **once Claude picks the skill**, not before. Set to `0` to turn the check off.

claudeViewer.budgets.skills.overrides.markdownDescription:
Per-skill budgets, keyed by skill name. Either field may be omitted — overriding one doesn't set the other.

```json
{ "dev-feature": { "content": 4000 } }
```

claudeViewer.context.warnAt.markdownDescription: Context size, in tokens, at which an agent's bar on the **Active Agents** surface turns yellow. An absolute count, not a share of the window — a 200k conversation is the same conversation whether the model holds 200k or 1M. Set to `0` to turn the warning off.

claudeViewer.context.errorAt.markdownDescription: Context size, in tokens, at which the bar turns red. Set to `0` to turn it off.

claudeViewer.context.windowFallback.markdownDescription: The context window assumed for a model Claude Viewer doesn't have a figure for. Windows aren't recorded in any file Claude Code writes, so they come from a small built-in table — this is what's used when the model isn't in it.

claudeViewer.context.window.markdownDescription:
Context window per model, keyed by the model id in the transcript. Overrules the built-in table, which is the way to correct an entry that's gone stale.

```json
{ "claude-opus-5": 1000000 }
```

claudeViewer.stages.names.markdownDescription:
What the session page's stage radars call each stage, keyed by the skill that opened it. Set these from **Assign names to stages** on a session page, or here.

```json
{ "dev-feature": "Build" }
```

enumDescriptions: Output tokens per skill. Measured by both CLIs, and the number Claude Code's own /usage reports.
What the turns cost: US dollars for Claude Code, priced from a table, and AIU for Copilot CLI, which records its own billed figure.
claudeViewer.usage.metric.markdownDescription: Which number the **Usage** surface reads. `output-tokens` is the only one with a single total across both CLIs — dollars and AIU are different units, so `cost` totals each CLI separately.

enumDescriptions: Every session on this machine, which is what usage limits are counted against.
Only sessions working under the open folder. A worktree under it counts as this workspace.
